newsitem.title: CHINA: China president woos Taiwan, pledges HK no change.
newsitem.headline: China president woos Taiwan, pledges HK no change.

text.p: Jubilant at resuming sovereignty over Hong Kong, China's President Jiang Zemin on Tuesday urged authorities in rival Taiwan to follow suit and reunify with a stronger, increasingly prosperous motherland.

In a speech broadcast live on state television from a rally to celebrate the handover of Hong Kong at midnight on Monday, Jiang reminded China's 1.2 billion people -- including those in Hong Kong -- of the triumph of the Communist Party in recovering the territory after 156 years of British colonial domination.

The state president and party chief tried to please both left and right in the powerful party hierarchy, paying tribute to communist China's founding fathers while promising his people, and those of capitalist Hong Kong, a prosperous future.
The "one country, two systems" formula devised by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping to recover Hong Kong without altering its freewheeling system was a model, Jiang said.
"It will set an example for...the final solution to the Taiwan question," he said, reminding rival Taiwan not to try to seek independence. Beijing regards the island as a rebel province.
"We hope that the Taiwan authorities will, setting store by the overall interests of our nation, truly return to the one China position," Jiang told the huge rally in Beijing's Workers' Stadium.
"We hope that the Taiwan authorities will... take concrete steps towards the development of cross-Straits relations and to the complete reunification of the country," he said.
It was China's most explicit suggestion to Taiwan since the Hong Kong handover hours earlier that it should follow Hong Kong's example since resuming sovereignty over Hong Kong.
"The prospect of complete national reunification... now stands promisingly in sight," Jiang said.

Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan, speaking minutes after Hong Kong's handover, said Taiwan could never accept communist rule. Reunification was possible only if all China, like Taiwan, adopts multiparty democracy -- a scheme Lien dubbed "one country, one good system".

Analysts say reunification is a key policy goal for China's leadership, which sees boosting patriotic sentiment among the population as a way to bolster communist credentials eroded by nearly two decades of market-style economic reform.

On the 76th birthday of the Chinese Communist Party, Jiang told his people that their prosperity, China's stability, the return of Hong Kong and a glittering future were possible only under communist rule.

Repeating again China's commitment to respect its agreement to leave Hong Kong untouched after the handover, Jiang promised also to push forward the economic reform policies of his late mentor Deng Xiaoping. He made no mention of political change although he assured Hong Kong it would enjoy gradual democracy.

Jiang smiled and even sang along during the rally when thousands of school children waved flags, hundreds of costumed dancers performed massive synchronised numbers and some of Hong Kong's and China's most famous pop stars crooned.
The show ended with a thundering display of 1,997 fireworks to celebrate the year in which Beijing recovered Hong Kong.
"The 100-year expectation of the Chinese people has finally come true," Jiang said.
